DeWitt’s mother’s family, the Snyders, were Schneiders from Lorraine.
Anton Laubacher was born at Montbronn, in the Moselle, in 1784, and at 48 he took his family to America:
they sailed from Le Havre on the Henri IV and landed at New York on 11 June 1832.
That border country had been fought over through a generation of Revolutionary and Napoleonic wars;
its farms were small and split among heirs, and the hungry years after the cold summer of 1816 sent thousands down
the Rhine to America. The Erie Canal, opened in 1825, carried them inland.
From 1827 Catholic families from Lorraine and Alsace were settling at Manlius Station,
on the canal east of Syracuse and now called Minoa, where they founded Saint Mary’s parish;
by 1838 Anthony Laubach was one of its trustees, with a Joseph Schneider.
John Nicholas Schneider, very probably born at Montbronn too, in 1814, married Anton’s daughter Mary Ann,
and their son Mathias was born at Minoa in 1849.
The census of 1850 found them at Manlius with eight children and Mary Ann’s widowed mother,
Margaret, who lived on with her daughter into her nineties.
Mathias married Maggie Seagfriet, whose parents had come from Luxembourg, and worked for the railroad;
in 1910 he was a railroad foreman, living in his own house at De Witt, outside Syracuse.
Mathias’s son William H. Snyder became a civil engineer for the federal government,
and the family lived in Syracuse, where Richard Snyder was born in 1927.
